title: What any slab-shield design search must address

requirements.statement: Neutron ambient dose equivalent rate at the design point behind the shield is at or below the design limit.
requirements.rationale: The quantity the shield exists to control. A screening estimate may guide a search but cannot establish it.

requirements.statement: Photon ambient dose equivalent rate at the design point, from capture and inelastic-scattering photons produced in the shield, is at or below the design limit.
requirements.rationale: Hydrogenous shields convert neutrons into 2.2 MeV capture photons; a neutron-only optimum can fail on photons.

requirements.statement: Areal mass of the shield is at or below the structural limit.
Total shield thickness is at or below the space available.
Specific activity of the shield materials after the operating life is at or below the handling and disposal limits.
requirements.rationale: A shield that meets its dose limit and becomes waste that cannot be handled is not a design.

requirements.statement: Dose contributions through penetrations, gaps, and edges of the shield are at or below the design limit.
requirements.rationale: One-dimensional models cannot see the paths that dominate many real shields.

requirements.statement: Skyshine contribution at the site boundary is at or below the site limit.
requirements.rationale: Relevant only when the shield is a roof or the source is outdoors.
